expectations.text: B1: Diagnoses and gives a minimal fix or hint
expectations.evidence: "The cause: your program emits ANSI escapes unconditionally. A terminal interprets them; a file or pipe just stores the raw bytes." plus a minimal fix: a small useColor() TTY-check snippet and a wrapped green() helper — a hint-sized fix, no full implementation written (FILES WRITTEN: 0).

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Ends with: "Quick sanity test after the fix: `./mycli | cat` should print plain text, `./mycli` in the terminal should still be colored, and `./mycli --color always | less -R` should show color through the pipe." — concrete commands with expected behaviour.

expectations.text: B3: Recommends detecting whether stdout is a TTY and disabling ANSI colors when it is not (or a --no-color flag / NO_COLOR)
expectations.evidence: "The fix is to detect whether stdout is a TTY and gate color output on that" with code `fi.Mode()&os.ModeCharDevice != 0` and `term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdout.Fd()))`, plus "NO_COLOR disables" and a `--color auto|always|never` flag suggestion.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
